title: Assortative mating can mask non-additive genetic contributions to individual differences
title_zh: 同类配偶可掩盖非加性遗传贡献导致的个体差异
abstract: Abstract Assortative mating impacts trait variation and covariation among individuals within populations. Here, we examine how direct and indirect assortative mating influence additive and non-additive genetic contributions to individual differences. In an extended twin design, we show by simulations that correlations between mating partners can mask non-additive genetic influences. Accounting for assortative mating can unmask non-additive genetic contributions, revealing upward biases in additive genetic estimates. We applied our approach to anthropometric (height), personality (openness to experience), and psychiatric (borderline personality disorder features) traits in a large dataset of 9000 Dutch families of twins, siblings, and spouses of twins. Our results demonstrate that accounting for partner correlations ( r = 0.21–0.29) unmasks non-additive genetic influences (13–19% of trait variation), leading to additive genetic estimates that are 14–39% smaller than those obtained from models ignoring assortment. Our findings clarify the impacts of assortative mating on both additive and non-additive genetic variance components, contributing to a better understanding of the heritability gap between twin and molecular-based studies, and highlight a refined framework for modelling the genetic transmission of behavioural and psychiatric traits.
abstract_zh: 摘要 同类配偶影响人群中个体间性状的变异及协变。本文考察直接和间接同类配偶如何影响加性和非加性遗传对个体差异的贡献。在扩展的双胞胎研究设计中，我们通过模拟表明，配偶间的相关性可掩盖非加性遗传影响。考虑同类配偶可揭示非加性遗传贡献，暴露出加性遗传估计值的向上偏倚。我们将该方法应用于大规模数据集中的9000个荷兰双胞胎、兄弟姐妹及双胞胎配偶家庭的人体测量（身高）、人格（体验开放性）和精神病学（边缘型人格障碍特征）性状。结果表明，考虑伴侣相关性（r = 0.21–0.29）可揭示非加性遗传影响（占性状变异的13–19%），导致加性遗传估计值比忽略同类配偶的模型小14–39%。本研究阐明了同类配偶对加性和非加性遗传方差成分的影响，有助于更好地理解双胞胎研究与基于分子遗传学的研究之间的遗传力差距，并为模拟行为和精神病性状的遗传传递提供了一个改进框架。
